cards.back: Engineering geology applies geological knowledge to civil engineering: site investigation, rock properties, and hazard assessment

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Geology
cards.back: Site investigation: desk study, walkover survey, boreholes, trial pits, geophysical surveys, and laboratory testing

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Geology
cards.back: Key rock properties: strength, permeability, porosity, discontinuities (joints, faults), and weathering grade

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Geology
cards.back: Foundation design depends on bearing capacity: strong bedrock supports heavy structures; weak clay requires deep foundations

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Geology
cards.back: Tunnelling must consider rock type, jointing, fault zones, groundwater and rock stress

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Geology
cards.back: Dams require impermeable foundations and strong abutments; geological mapping is essential before construction

cards.front: What should you know about gcse geology exam tips — engineering geology?
cards.back: 1. For Engineering Geology questions, use correct geological terminology and classify features precisely 2. Reference specific geological time periods and processes 3. When interpreting data, consider the quality and limitations of the evidence 4. Apply your understanding of Engineering Geology to fieldwork observations and map data 5. For evaluation, weigh competing geological theories with evidence
